title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on the Limitation Period for Guarantee Acts Occurring Before the Effectiveness of the Guarantee Law
keywords_en: contract dispute; bankruptcy; guarantee; surety; statute of limitations
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issues Concerning the Limitation Period for Guarantee Actions Occurring Prior to the Effectiveness of the Guarantee Law

Fa [2002] No. 144

To: the Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region

After our court promulgated Fa Shi [2000] No. 44, the "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China," on December 8, 2000, some departments and local courts reported that no provisions had been made on how to determine the guarantee period for guarantee actions occurring before the implementation of the Guarantee Law, and that our court's Fa Fa [1994] No. 8, the "Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Economic Contract Dispute Cases Involving Guarantees," promulgated on April 15, 1994, was also not sufficiently clear on this issue. In order to properly adjudicate cases involving disputes over guarantee contracts concluded before the implementation of the Guarantee Law and to protect the lawful rights and interests of creditors and other interested parties, after consultation with and approval of the Legislative Affairs Commission of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, we hereby notify you of the relevant issues as follows:

1. Where a guarantee contract concluded by the parties prior to the effectiveness of the Guarantee Law did not stipulate a guarantee period or the stipulation was unclear, if the creditor has already asserted its rights against the principal debtor within the statutory limitation period, so that the principal debt has not exceeded the limitation period, but has not yet asserted its rights against the guarantor, the creditor may assert its rights against the guarantor within six months from the date of issuance of this Notice (from August 1, 2002 to January 31, 2003). If the creditor fails to assert its rights within that period, the guarantor shall no longer bear liability.

2. Where the principal debtor has entered bankruptcy proceedings and the creditor has not declared its claim, the creditor may also assert its claim against the guarantor within the aforementioned period. If the creditor has declared its claim, the creditor may, with respect to the portion of its claim not satisfied in the bankruptcy proceedings, assert its claim against the guarantor within six months after the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings.

3. This Notice shall not apply to cases that have already been finally adjudicated, cases under retrial, or cases where the principal debt has already exceeded the limitation period at the time of issuance of this Notice.

August 1, 2002
